title.zh: 卷36 列傳第1 后妃
title.raw: 卷36 列傳第1 后妃 Volume 36 Biographies 1: Empresses and Consorts

sentences.zh: 夫陰陽肇分，乾坤定位，君臣之道斯著，夫婦之義存焉。

translations.literal: When yin and yang first divided, heaven and earth took their places; the way of ruler and minister was thereby made manifest, and the meaning of husband and wife was established.
translations.idiomatic: When yin and yang first separated and heaven and earth took their fixed places, the bond between ruler and minister came into view, and the duties of husband and wife were set in place.

sentences.zh: 陰陽和則裁成萬物，家道正則化行天下，由近及遠，自家刑國，配天作合，不亦大乎！

translations.literal: When yin and yang are in harmony, the myriad things are fashioned; when the way of the household is correct, transformation spreads through the realm—from near to far, from family to state, matching heaven in union—is this not great!
translations.idiomatic: When yin and yang are in harmony, the myriad things take shape; when the household is rightly ordered, its influence reaches the whole realm. From the family to the state, from what is near to what is far—union with heaven in marriage—is this not a matter of the greatest weight?

sentences.zh: 興亡是繫，不亦重乎！

translations.literal: Rise and fall depend upon it—is this not weighty!
translations.idiomatic: Upon it the rise and fall of dynasties depend—is this not grave indeed!

sentences.zh: 是以先王慎之，正其本而嚴其防。

translations.literal: Therefore the former kings were cautious regarding it, rectifying the root and making strict the defenses.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the ancient kings treated the matter with care, setting the foundation aright and guarding the barriers with strictness.

sentences.zh: 後之繼體，靡克聿修，甘心柔曼之容，罔念幽閑之操。

translations.literal: Later heirs to the throne mostly could not continue the tradition, content with soft and alluring looks, heedless of quiet and modest conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Later rulers who inherited the throne seldom carried on the tradition; they were content with soft, alluring beauty and gave no thought to quiet, modest virtue.

sentences.zh: 成敗攸屬，安危斯在。

translations.literal: Success and failure depend upon it; security and peril lie therein.
translations.idiomatic: Victory and defeat hang upon it; safety and danger rest upon it as well.

sentences.zh: 故皇、英降而虞道隆，任、姒歸而姬宗盛，妹、妲致夏、殷之釁，褒、趙結周、漢之禍。

translations.literal: Thus when Huang and Ying descended, the way of Yu flourished; when Ren and Si came home, the Ji clan prospered; Mei and Da brought the calamities of Xia and Yin, Bao and Zhao sealed the disasters of Zhou and Han.
translations.idiomatic: When E Huang and Nüying came down to Shun, the way of Yu flourished; when Ren and Si entered the Zhou house, the Ji clan rose to greatness. Mei Xi and Daji brought ruin upon Xia and Yin; Bao Si and Zhao Feiyan brought disaster upon Zhou and Han.

sentences.zh: 爰歷晉、宋，實繁有徒。

translations.literal: Continuing through Jin and Song, there were indeed many such cases.
translations.idiomatic: Down through Jin and Song, examples of this kind were truly numerous.

sentences.zh: 皆位以寵升，榮非德進，恣行淫僻，莫顧禮儀，為梟為鴟，敗不旋踵。

translations.literal: All rose in rank through favor, their glory gained not through virtue; they indulged in wanton and perverse conduct, heedless of ritual propriety—becoming owls and kites, their ruin came without turning the heel.
translations.idiomatic: They all advanced through imperial favor rather than merit, abandoned themselves to licentious and perverse conduct, and cared nothing for ritual propriety. Like owls and kites among birds, they met ruin almost at once.

sentences.zh: 後之伉儷宸極，正位居中，罕蹈平易之塗，多遵覆車之轍。

translations.literal: Later consorts of the imperial apex, occupying the central position, rarely trod the level path and mostly followed the tracks of overturned carts.
translations.idiomatic: Later empresses who shared the imperial throne and sat in the central place seldom took the easy road; far more often they followed the tracks of overturned carts.

sentences.zh: 睢鳩之德，千載寂寥；

translations.literal: The virtue of the osprey, for a thousand years lonely and still;
translations.idiomatic: The virtue praised in the Ospreys lay silent for a thousand years;

sentences.zh: 牝雞之晨，殊邦接響。

translations.literal: the hen's morning crowing, in distant states echo answered echo.
translations.idiomatic: while the hen's crowing at dawn echoed from one foreign land to the next.

sentences.zh: 窈窕淑女，靡有求於寤寐；

translations.literal: Fair and gentle ladies—none sought in waking and sleep;
translations.idiomatic: Fair and gentle ladies were no longer sought in waking thought and in dreams;

sentences.zh: 鏗鏘環珮，鮮克嗣於徽音。

translations.literal: resounding pendants and rings—few could continue the excellent reputation.
translations.idiomatic: and though jade pendants chimed at their belts, few could carry on the fame of worthy wives.

sentences.zh: 永念前修，歎深彤管。

translations.literal: Ever mindful of former exemplars, I sigh deeply over the red tube.
translations.idiomatic: Ever mindful of the worthy women of old, I sigh deeply over the red brush that should have recorded their praise.

sentences.zh: 覽載籍於既往，考行事於當時，存亡得失之機，蓋亦多矣。

translations.literal: Perusing the records of the past and examining conduct in the present, the springs of survival, extinction, gain, and loss are indeed many.
translations.idiomatic: In reviewing the records of the past and weighing conduct in the present, one finds that the turning points of survival and ruin, gain and loss, are many indeed.

sentences.zh: 故述皇后列傳，所以垂戒將來。

translations.literal: Therefore I set forth the collective biography of empresses, in order to leave a warning for those to come.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I compose this collective biography of empresses—to leave a warning for generations yet to come.

sentences.zh: 然后妃之制，夏、殷以前略矣。

translations.literal: As for the institution of empresses and consorts, before Xia and Yin it was only sketched in outline.
translations.idiomatic: As for the institution governing empresses and consorts, before the Xia and Yin dynasties it existed only in rough outline.

sentences.zh: 周公定禮，內職始備列焉。

translations.literal: When the Duke of Zhou fixed the rites, the inner offices first took full array.
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke of Zhou established the rites, the inner palace offices were first set out in full array.

sentences.zh: 秦、漢以下，代有沿革，品秩差次，前史載之詳矣。

translations.literal: From Qin and Han downward, each age had its reforms; ranks and grades differed in order—the former histories record these in detail.
translations.idiomatic: From Qin and Han onward, each dynasty revised the system, and the gradations of rank differed from age to age; the earlier histories record all this in detail.

sentences.zh: 齊、梁以降，歷魏暨周，廢置益損，參差不一。

translations.literal: From Qi and Liang downward, through Wei and on to Zhou, abolitions and establishments increased and diminished, uneven and not uniform.
translations.idiomatic: From Qi and Liang through Wei and into Zhou, offices were abolished and restored, expanded and cut back, in ways that were uneven and inconsistent.

sentences.zh: 周宣嗣位，不率典章，衣褘翟、稱中宮者，凡有五。

translations.literal: When Xuan of Zhou succeeded to the throne, he did not follow the statutes; those who wore the hui and di robes and were called Central Palace numbered five in all.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan of Northern Zhou succeeded to the throne, he did not follow the canonical regulations: five women in all wore the empress's hui and di robes and were styled ladies of the Central Palace.

sentences.zh: 夫人以下，略無定數。

translations.literal: Below the rank of Lady, there was scarcely any fixed number.
translations.idiomatic: Below the rank of Lady, there was scarcely any fixed quota at all.

sentences.zh: 高祖思革前弊，大矯其違，唯皇后正位，傍無私寵，婦官稱號，未詳備焉。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor wished to reform the abuses of earlier times and greatly correct their deviations; only the empress held the orthodox position, with no private favorites at her side, while titles for palace women were not yet fully detailed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen wished to reform the abuses of earlier ages and to correct their excesses in full. Only the empress held the legitimate position, with no private favorites beside her, while the titles for palace women had not yet been worked out in complete detail.

sentences.zh: 開皇二年，著內官之式，略依周禮，省減其數。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaihuang, he set down the pattern for inner officials, following in outline the Rites of Zhou and reducing their number.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaihuang (582), he promulgated the regulations for inner palace officials, following the Rites of Zhou in broad outline and reducing the number of posts.

sentences.zh: 嬪三員，掌教四德，視正三品。

translations.literal: Three Pin, who supervised instruction in the four virtues, ranked equal to regular third grade.
translations.idiomatic: Three Pin, who supervised instruction in the four virtues, were ranked equal to regular third grade.

sentences.zh: 世婦九員，掌賓客祭祀，視正五品。

translations.literal: Nine Shifu, who managed guests and sacrifices, ranked equal to regular fifth grade.
translations.idiomatic: Nine Shifu, who managed guests and sacrifices, were ranked equal to regular fifth grade.

sentences.zh: 女御三十八員，掌女工絲枲，視正七品。

translations.literal: Thirty-eight Nuyu, who managed women's work in silk and hemp, ranked equal to regular seventh grade.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-eight Nuyu, who supervised women's work in silk and hemp, were ranked equal to regular seventh grade.

sentences.zh: 又採漢、晉舊儀，置六尚、六司、六典，遞相統攝，以掌宮掖之政。

translations.literal: He also drew on the old regulations of Han and Jin, establishing the Six Chiefs, Six Directors, and Six Registrars, each supervising the next in turn, to administer the affairs of the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: He also drew on the old regulations of Han and Jin and established the Six Chiefs, Six Directors, and Six Registrars, each level supervising the next, to govern affairs within the palace.

sentences.zh: 一曰尚宮，掌導引皇后及閨閤廩賜。

translations.literal: The first was Chief of the Palace, who managed guiding the empress and the granary gifts of the inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The first was the Chief of the Palace, who guided the empress and managed granary distributions within the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 管司令三人，掌圖籍法式，糾察宣奏；

translations.literal: under whom were three Directors of Orders, who managed maps, registers, statutes, and patterns, and who inspected and announced memorials;
translations.idiomatic: Under her were three Directors of Orders, who managed maps, registers, statutes, and patterns and who inspected and forwarded memorials;

sentences.zh: 典琮三人，掌琮璽器玩。

translations.literal: and three Registrars of the Jade Tablet, who managed jade tablets, seals, vessels, and curios.
translations.idiomatic: and three Registrars of the Jade Tablet, who managed jade tablets, seals, vessels, and precious objects.

sentences.zh: 二曰尚儀，掌禮儀教學。

translations.literal: The second was Chief of Ceremonies, who managed ritual and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: The second was the Chief of Ceremonies, who managed ritual and instruction.

sentences.zh: 管司樂三人，掌音律之事；

translations.literal: under whom were three Directors of Music, who managed matters of pitch and regulation;
translations.idiomatic: Under her were three Directors of Music, who managed matters of pitch and regulation;

sentences.zh: 典贊三人，掌導引內外命婦朝見。

translations.literal: and three Registrars of Presentation, who managed guiding inner and outer titled ladies in audience.
translations.idiomatic: and three Registrars of Presentation, who guided titled ladies of the inner and outer courts in their audiences.

sentences.zh: 三曰尚服，掌服章寶藏。

translations.literal: The third was Chief of Vestments, who managed garments, insignia, and the treasure store.
translations.idiomatic: The third was the Chief of Vestments, who managed garments, insignia, and the treasure store.

sentences.zh: 管司飾三人，掌簪珥花嚴；

translations.literal: under whom were three Directors of Adornment, who managed hairpins, earrings, flowers, and formal dress;
translations.idiomatic: Under her were three Directors of Adornment, who managed hairpins, earrings, flowers, and formal dress;

sentences.zh: 典櫛三人，掌巾櫛膏沐。

translations.literal: and three Registrars of the Comb, who managed towels, combs, oils, and bathing.
translations.idiomatic: and three Registrars of the Comb, who managed towels, combs, oils, and bathing.

sentences.zh: 四曰尚食，掌進膳先嘗。

translations.literal: The fourth was Chief of Provisions, who managed presenting food and tasting it first.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth was the Chief of Provisions, who managed the presentation of food and tasted it before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 管司醫三人，掌方藥卜筮；

translations.literal: under whom were three Directors of Medicine, who managed prescriptions, drugs, divination, and milfoil;
translations.idiomatic: Under her were three Directors of Medicine, who managed prescriptions, drugs, divination, and milfoil;

sentences.zh: 典器三人，掌樽彝器皿。

translations.literal: and three Registrars of Vessels, who managed goblets, sacrificial bronzes, and utensils.
translations.idiomatic: and three Registrars of Vessels, who managed goblets, sacrificial bronzes, and serving vessels.

sentences.zh: 五曰尚寢，掌幃帳牀褥。

translations.literal: The fifth was Chief of the Bedchamber, who managed curtains, canopies, beds, and bedding.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth was the Chief of the Bedchamber, who managed curtains, canopies, beds, and bedding.

sentences.zh: 管司筵三人，掌鋪設灑掃；

translations.literal: under whom were three Directors of Mats, who managed spreading furnishings and sprinkling and sweeping;
translations.idiomatic: Under her were three Directors of Mats, who managed furnishings, sprinkling, and sweeping;

sentences.zh: 典執三人，掌扇傘燈燭。

translations.literal: and three Registrars of Attendants, who managed fans, parasols, lamps, and candles.
translations.idiomatic: and three Registrars of Attendants, who managed fans, parasols, lamps, and candles.

sentences.zh: 六曰尚工，掌營造百役。

translations.literal: The sixth was Chief of Works, who managed construction and the hundred tasks.
translations.idiomatic: The sixth was the Chief of Works, who managed construction and the hundred crafts.

sentences.zh: 管司製三人，掌衣服裁縫；

translations.literal: under whom were three Directors of Tailoring, who managed garments, cutting, and sewing;
translations.idiomatic: Under her were three Directors of Tailoring, who managed garments, cutting, and sewing;

sentences.zh: 典會三人，掌財帛出入。

translations.literal: and three Registrars of Accounts, who managed the receipt and disbursement of valuables and silks.
translations.idiomatic: and three Registrars of Accounts, who managed the receipt and disbursement of valuables and silks.

sentences.zh: 六尚各三員，視從九品，六司視勳品，六典視流外二品。

translations.literal: Each of the Six Chiefs had three posts, ranked equal to subordinate ninth grade; the Six Directors were ranked equal to merit grades; the Six Registrars were ranked equal to outside-the-register second grade.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the Six Chiefs numbered three posts and was ranked equal to subordinate ninth grade; the Six Directors were ranked as merit grades; the Six Registrars were ranked as outside-the-register second grade.

sentences.zh: 初，文獻皇后功參歷試，外預朝政，內擅宮闈，懷嫉妬之心，虛嬪妾之位，不設三妃，防其上逼。

translations.literal: At first Empress Wenxian's merit shared in the trials of the age; outwardly she took part in court government, inwardly she monopolized the inner palace. Harboring a jealous heart, she left the posts of concubines vacant and did not establish the Three Consorts, guarding against being pressed from above.
translations.idiomatic: At first Empress Wenxian had shared in her husband's rise to power. She took part in court politics and dominated the inner palace. Jealous by nature, she left the posts of concubines empty, did not establish the Three Consorts, and guarded against any rival who might press upon her from above.

sentences.zh: 自嬪以下，置六十員。

translations.literal: From Pin downward, sixty posts were established.
translations.idiomatic: From the rank of Pin downward, only sixty posts were established in all.

sentences.zh: 加又抑損服章，降其品秩。

translations.literal: Moreover she further reduced insignia on garments and lowered their grades.
translations.idiomatic: She further reduced the insignia on their garments and lowered their ranks.

sentences.zh: 至文獻崩後，始置貴人三員，增嬪至九員，世婦二十七員，御女八十一員。

translations.literal: Only after Wenxian's death were three Noble Ladies first established; Pin were increased to nine, Shifu to twenty-seven, and Imperial Women to eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Empress Wenxian's death were three Noble Ladies first established; the Pin were increased to nine, the Shifu to twenty-seven, and the Imperial Women to eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 貴人等關掌宮闈之務，六尚已下，皆分隸焉。

translations.literal: The Noble Ladies and others supervised the affairs of the inner palace; from the Six Chiefs downward, all were placed under them in separate subordination.
translations.idiomatic: The Noble Ladies and their subordinates supervised affairs within the palace, and from the Six Chiefs downward all were placed under them.

sentences.zh: 煬帝時，后妃嬪御，無釐婦職，唯端容麗飾，陪從醼遊而已。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Yang, empresses, consorts, Pin, and attendants did not put in order women's duties; they only composed their appearance with fine adornment and accompanied banquets and excursions.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yang, empresses, consorts, and palace women no longer performed the duties of wives; they merely dressed their faces, arrayed themselves in finery, and accompanied the emperor at banquets and excursions.

sentences.zh: 帝又參詳典故，自製嘉名，著之於令。

translations.literal: The emperor also consulted and examined ancient precedents, devised fine names himself, and set them down in edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also studied ancient precedents, devised elegant titles of his own, and set them down in edict.

sentences.zh: 貴妃、淑妃、德妃，是為三夫人，品正第一。

translations.literal: Imperial Consort, Pure Consort, and Virtuous Consort—these were the Three Ladies, of orthodox first rank.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Consort, Pure Consort, and Virtuous Consort—these were the Three Ladies, of orthodox first rank.

sentences.zh: 順儀、順容、順華、修儀、修容、修華、充儀、充容、充華，是為九嬪，品正第二。

translations.literal: Compliant Form, Compliant Countenance, Compliant Splendor, Cultivated Form, Cultivated Countenance, Cultivated Splendor, Fulfilling Form, Fulfilling Countenance, and Fulfilling Splendor—these were the Nine Pin, of orthodox second rank.
translations.idiomatic: Compliant Form, Compliant Countenance, Compliant Splendor, Cultivated Form, Cultivated Countenance, Cultivated Splendor, Fulfilling Form, Fulfilling Countenance, and Fulfilling Splendor—these were the Nine Pin, of orthodox second rank.

sentences.zh: 婕妤一十二員，品正第三，美人、才人一十五員，品正第四，是為世婦。

translations.literal: Twelve Ladies of Handsome Fairness, of orthodox third rank; fifteen Beauties and fifteen Talented Ladies, of orthodox fourth rank—these were the Shifu.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve Ladies of Handsome Fairness of orthodox third rank; fifteen Beauties and fifteen Talented Ladies of orthodox fourth rank—these constituted the Shifu.

sentences.zh: 寶林二十四員，品正第五；

translations.literal: Twenty-four Treasured Forest attendants, of orthodox fifth rank;
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-four Treasured Forest attendants of orthodox fifth rank;

sentences.zh: 御女二十四員，品正第六；

translations.literal: twenty-four Imperial Women, of orthodox sixth rank;
translations.idiomatic: twenty-four Imperial Women of orthodox sixth rank;

sentences.zh: 采女三十七員，品正第七，是為女御。

translations.literal: thirty-seven Selected Women, of orthodox seventh rank—these were the Nuyu.
translations.idiomatic: and thirty-seven Selected Women of orthodox seventh rank—these were the Nuyu.

sentences.zh: 總一百二十，以叙於宴寢。

translations.literal: In all one hundred twenty, arranged in order for banquets and bedchambers.
translations.idiomatic: In all there were one hundred twenty, ranked in order for banquets and the bedchamber.

sentences.zh: 又有承衣刀人，皆趨侍左右，並無員數，視六品已下。

translations.literal: There were also robe-bearers and blade-women, all hurrying to attend at left and right, with no fixed quota, ranked below sixth grade.
translations.idiomatic: There were also robe-bearers and blade-women, all of whom hurried to wait upon him at his side; they had no fixed quota and were ranked below sixth grade.

sentences.zh: 時又增置女官，準尚書省，以六局管二十四司。

translations.literal: At that time female officials were also added, modeled on the Department of State Affairs, with six bureaus administering twenty-four offices.
translations.idiomatic: At that time female officials were also added, modeled on the Department of State Affairs, with six bureaus administering twenty-four offices.

sentences.zh: 一曰尚宮局，管司言，掌宣傳奏啟；

translations.literal: The first was the Bureau of the Palace, which supervised the Office of Speech and managed proclaiming, transmitting, memorializing, and reporting;
translations.idiomatic: The first was the Bureau of the Palace, which supervised the Office of Speech and managed proclamations, transmissions, memorials, and reports;

sentences.zh: 司簿，掌名錄計度；

translations.literal: the Office of Registers, which managed name lists and reckoning;
translations.idiomatic: the Office of Registers, which managed name lists and accounts;

sentences.zh: 司正，掌格式推罰；

translations.literal: the Office of Rectification, which managed forms, standards, investigation, and punishment;
translations.idiomatic: the Office of Rectification, which managed regulations, investigation, and punishment;

sentences.zh: 司闈，掌門閤管鑰。

translations.literal: and the Office of the Gate, which managed doors, side gates, and keys.
translations.idiomatic: and the Office of the Gate, which managed doors, side gates, and keys.

sentences.zh: 二曰尚儀局，管司籍，掌經史教學，紙筆几案；

translations.literal: The second was the Bureau of Ceremonies, which supervised the Office of Registers and managed the classics and histories, instruction, paper, brushes, and desks;
translations.idiomatic: The second was the Bureau of Ceremonies, which supervised the Office of the Classics and managed the canon, histories, instruction, paper, brushes, and desks;

sentences.zh: 司樂，掌音律；

translations.literal: the Office of Music, which managed pitch and regulation;
translations.idiomatic: the Office of Music, which managed pitch and regulation;

sentences.zh: 司賓，掌賓客；

translations.literal: the Office of Guests, which managed guests;
translations.idiomatic: the Office of Guests, which managed guests;

sentences.zh: 司贊，掌禮儀贊相導引。

translations.literal: and the Office of Presentation, which managed ritual, assisting, and guiding.
translations.idiomatic: and the Office of Presentation, which managed ritual assistance and guidance.

sentences.zh: 三曰尚服局，管司璽，掌琮璽符節；

translations.literal: The third was the Bureau of Vestments, which supervised the Office of the Seal and managed jade tablets, seals, tallies, and insignia;
translations.idiomatic: The third was the Bureau of Vestments, which supervised the Office of the Seal and managed jade tablets, seals, tallies, and insignia;

sentences.zh: 司衣，掌衣服；

translations.literal: the Office of Garments, which managed clothing;
translations.idiomatic: the Office of Garments, which managed clothing;

sentences.zh: 司飾，掌湯沐巾櫛玩弄；

translations.literal: the Office of Adornment, which managed hot water, bathing, towels, combs, and playthings;
translations.idiomatic: the Office of Adornment, which managed bathing, towels, combs, and personal ornaments;

sentences.zh: 司仗，掌仗衞戎器。

translations.literal: and the Office of Arms, which managed guards of honor, escorts, and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: and the Office of Arms, which managed guards of honor, escorts, and weapons.

sentences.zh: 四曰尚食局，管司膳，掌膳羞；

translations.literal: The fourth was the Bureau of Provisions, which supervised the Office of Meals and managed food and delicacies;
translations.idiomatic: The fourth was the Bureau of Provisions, which supervised the Office of Meals and managed food and delicacies;

sentences.zh: 司醞，掌酒醴醯醢；

translations.literal: the Office of Brewing, which managed wine, sweet wine, vinegar, and pickled meats;
translations.idiomatic: the Office of Brewing, which managed wine, sweet wine, vinegar, and pickled meats;

sentences.zh: 司藥，掌醫巫藥劑；

translations.literal: the Office of Medicine, which managed physicians, shamans, and drugs;
translations.idiomatic: the Office of Medicine, which managed physicians, shamans, and drugs;

sentences.zh: 司饎，掌廩餼柴炭。

translations.literal: and the Office of Rations, which managed granaries, provisions, firewood, and charcoal.
translations.idiomatic: and the Office of Rations, which managed granaries, provisions, firewood, and charcoal.

sentences.zh: 五曰尚寢局，管司設，掌牀席帷帳，鋪設灑掃；

translations.literal: The fifth was the Bureau of the Bedchamber, which supervised the Office of Furnishings and managed beds, mats, curtains, and canopies, spreading furnishings and sprinkling and sweeping;
translations.idiomatic: The fifth was the Bureau of the Bedchamber, which supervised the Office of Furnishings and managed beds, mats, curtains, and canopies, as well as spreading furnishings and cleaning;

sentences.zh: 司輿，掌輿輦傘扇，執持羽儀；

translations.literal: the Office of Carriages, which managed palanquins, carriages, parasols, and fans, holding feathered insignia;
translations.idiomatic: the Office of Carriages, which managed palanquins, carriages, parasols, and fans and bore feathered insignia;

sentences.zh: 司苑，掌園籞種植，蔬菜瓜果；

translations.literal: the Office of Parks, which managed gardens, enclosures, planting, vegetables, and melons;
translations.idiomatic: the Office of Parks, which managed gardens, planting, vegetables, and melons;

sentences.zh: 司燈，掌火燭。

translations.literal: and the Office of Lamps, which managed fire and candles.
translations.idiomatic: and the Office of Lamps, which managed fire and candles.

sentences.zh: 六曰尚工局，管司製，掌營造裁縫，司寶，掌金玉珠璣錢貨；

translations.literal: The sixth was the Bureau of Works, which supervised the Office of Manufacture and managed construction and tailoring; the Office of Treasures, which managed gold, jade, pearls, disks, and currency;
translations.idiomatic: The sixth was the Bureau of Works, which supervised the Office of Manufacture and managed construction and tailoring; the Office of Treasures, which managed gold, jade, pearls, disks, and currency;

sentences.zh: 司綵，掌繒帛；

translations.literal: the Office of Colors, which managed silks and brocades;
translations.idiomatic: the Office of Colors, which managed silks and brocades;

sentences.zh: 司織，掌織染。

translations.literal: and the Office of Weaving, which managed weaving and dyeing.
translations.idiomatic: and the Office of Weaving, which managed weaving and dyeing.

sentences.zh: 六尚二十二司，員各二人，唯司樂、司膳員各四人。

translations.literal: Of the Six Chiefs' twenty-two offices, each had two posts; only the Offices of Music and of Meals had four posts each.
translations.idiomatic: Of the twenty-two offices under the Six Chiefs, each had two posts; only the Offices of Music and of Meals had four posts each.

sentences.zh: 每司又置典及掌，以貳其職。

translations.literal: Each office also had Registrars and Assistants placed to share its duties.
translations.idiomatic: Each office also had Registrars and Assistants to share its duties.

sentences.zh: 六尚十人，品從第五；

translations.literal: Ten Chiefs, of subordinate fifth rank;
translations.idiomatic: Ten Chiefs of subordinate fifth rank;

sentences.zh: 司二十八人，品從第六；

translations.literal: twenty-eight Directors, of subordinate sixth rank;
translations.idiomatic: twenty-eight Directors of subordinate sixth rank;

sentences.zh: 典二十八人，品從第七；

translations.literal: twenty-eight Registrars, of subordinate seventh rank;
translations.idiomatic: twenty-eight Registrars of subordinate seventh rank;

sentences.zh: 掌二十八人，品從第九。

translations.literal: and twenty-eight Assistants, of subordinate ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: and twenty-eight Assistants of subordinate ninth rank.

sentences.zh: 女使流外，量局閑劇，多者十人已下，無定員數。

translations.literal: Female envoys outside the register were allotted according to whether a bureau was idle or busy; where many were needed, ten or fewer, with no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Female attendants outside the regular register were assigned according to whether a bureau was busy or idle; where many were needed, there might be as many as ten, but there was no fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 聯事分職，各有司存焉。

translations.literal: Linked duties were divided among offices, each with its own charge.
translations.idiomatic: Duties were linked and divided among offices, each with its own charge.

sentences.zh: 文獻獨孤皇后，河南洛陽人，周大司馬、河內公信之女也。

translations.literal: Empress Wenxian of the Dugu clan was a native of Luoyang in Henan, daughter of Xin, Grand Marshal of Zhou and Duke of Hanoi.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wenxian of the Dugu clan was a native of Luoyang in Henan, daughter of Dugu Xin, Grand Marshal of Zhou and Duke of Hanoi.

sentences.zh: 信見高祖有奇表，故以后妻焉，時年十四。

translations.literal: Xin saw that the Founding Emperor had an extraordinary appearance and therefore gave him his daughter as wife; she was then fourteen.
translations.idiomatic: When Dugu Xin saw that the future Emperor Wen had an extraordinary appearance, he gave him his daughter in marriage; she was then fourteen.

sentences.zh: 高祖與后相得，誓無異生之子。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor and the empress were well matched; they swore there would be no sons born to another.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen and the empress were deeply devoted to each other and swore that they would have no sons by any other woman.

sentences.zh: 后初亦柔順恭孝，不失婦道。

translations.literal: At first the empress was also gentle, compliant, respectful, and filial, not failing in the way of a wife.
translations.idiomatic: At first the empress was gentle, compliant, respectful, and filial and did not fall short in the duties of a wife.

sentences.zh: 后姊為周明帝后，長女為周宣帝后，貴戚之盛，莫與為比，而后每謙卑自守，世以為賢。

translations.literal: The empress's elder sister was empress to Ming of Zhou, and her eldest daughter was empress to Xuan of Zhou; no kin by marriage was more exalted, yet the empress always kept herself humble and restrained, and the age considered her worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Her elder sister was empress to Emperor Ming of Northern Zhou, and her eldest daughter became empress to Emperor Xuan; no consort kin in the realm was more exalted. Yet the empress always kept herself humble and restrained, and the world regarded her as worthy.

sentences.zh: 及周宣帝崩，高祖居禁中，總百揆，后使人謂高祖曰：「大事已然，騎獸之勢，必不得下，勉之！

translations.literal: When Xuan of Zhou died, the Founding Emperor dwelt in the forbidden precincts and oversaw all affairs of state. The empress sent someone to tell him: "The great matter is already settled. Once you are mounted on a beast, you cannot come down—press on!"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan of Northern Zhou died, Emperor Wen remained within the palace and took charge of all government affairs. The empress sent word to him: "The decisive moment has come. Once you are mounted on a beast, you cannot dismount—press forward!"

sentences.zh: 」高祖受禪，立為皇后。

translations.literal: " The Founding Emperor received the abdication and established her as empress.
translations.idiomatic: " When he accepted the abdication and took the throne, he installed her as empress.

sentences.zh: 突厥嘗與中國交市，有明珠一篋，價值八百萬，幽州總管陰壽白后市之。

translations.literal: The Turks once traded with China; there was a casket of bright pearls worth eight million, and Yin Shou, regional commander of Youzhou, reported to the empress that she might purchase them.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks once traded with China, and a casket of luminous pearls worth eight million came on the market. Yin Shou, regional commander of Youzhou, reported to the empress that she might buy them.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「非我所須也。

translations.literal: The empress said: "These are not what I need.
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "These are not what I need.

sentences.zh: 當今戎狄屢寇，將士罷勞，未若以八百萬分賞有功者。

translations.literal: Nowadays the barbarians raid repeatedly and the officers and soldiers are weary and worn. Would it not be better to divide the eight million and reward those who have merit?"
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians raid us again and again, and our officers and soldiers are worn out with labor. Would it not be better to divide the eight million and reward those who have served with merit?"

sentences.zh: 」百僚聞而畢賀。

translations.literal: " When the hundred officials heard this, all congratulated her.
translations.idiomatic: " When the officials heard this, all congratulated her.

sentences.zh: 高祖甚寵憚之。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor greatly favored and feared her.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen both cherished and stood in awe of her.

sentences.zh: 上每臨朝，后輒與上方輦而進，至閣乃止。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor attended court, the empress would ride in the same carriage with him and advance together, stopping only when they reached the gate-tower.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor went to court, the empress rode in the same carriage with him and went as far as the gate-tower before stopping.

sentences.zh: 使宦官伺上，政有所失，隨則匡諫，多所弘益。

translations.literal: She had eunuchs watch the emperor; whenever his governance went astray, she would immediately correct and remonstrate with him, and much was thereby enlarged and benefited.
translations.idiomatic: She had eunuchs watch him in court, and whenever his governance went astray she would remonstrate with him at once. Much good came of this.

sentences.zh: 候上退朝而同反燕寢，相顧欣然。

translations.literal: She waited for the emperor to leave court and returned with him to the private apartments, gazing at each other with pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: She waited for him to leave court and returned with him to the private apartments, where they would look at each other with quiet delight.

sentences.zh: 后早失二親，常懷感慕，見公卿有父母者，每為致禮焉。

translations.literal: The empress had early lost both parents and always cherished feelings of longing and admiration; when she saw high ministers who still had parents, she would each time extend courtesy to them on that account.
translations.idiomatic: The empress had lost both parents early in life and always cherished their memory. Whenever she saw a high minister who still had living parents, she would extend special courtesy to him.

sentences.zh: 有司奏以周禮百官之妻，命於王后，憲章在昔，請依古制。

translations.literal: The responsible offices memorialized that according to the Rites of Zhou the wives of the hundred officials received their appointments from the queen, and that the statutes of old stood on record; they asked to follow the ancient system.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices memorialized that, according to the Rites of Zhou, the wives of officials received their appointments from the queen, and that precedent from antiquity supported this; they asked to follow the ancient system.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「以婦人與政，或從此漸，不可開其源也。

translations.literal: The empress said: "To let women share in government may begin gradually from this—one must not open the source of it."
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "If women are allowed to share in government, the practice may spread from this beginning. The source of such a change must not be opened."

sentences.zh: 」不許。

translations.literal: " She did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: " She did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 后每謂諸公主曰：「周家公主，類無婦德，失禮於舅姑，離薄人骨肉，此不順事，爾等當誡之。

translations.literal: The empress often told the princesses: "The princesses of the Zhou house for the most part lacked wifely virtue, were disrespectful to parents-in-law, and estranged and pitted kin against kin. These are unfitting acts—you must take warning from them."
translations.idiomatic: The empress often told the princesses, "The princesses of the Zhou house for the most part lacked wifely virtue. They were disrespectful to their parents-in-law and drove wedges between close kin. These are unfitting acts, and you must take warning from them."

sentences.zh: 」大都督崔長仁，后之中外兄弟也，犯法當斬。

translations.literal: " Grand Commander Cui Changren, a brother of the empress on both her father's and mother's sides, violated the law and should be beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: " Grand Commander Cui Changren, a brother of the empress on both her father's and mother's sides, broke the law and was sentenced to execution.

sentences.zh: 高祖以后之故，欲免其罪。

translations.literal: Because of the empress, the Founding Emperor wished to spare him punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Because of the empress, Emperor Wen wished to spare him.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「國家之事，焉可顧私！

translations.literal: The empress said: "Matters of the state—how can one look to private ties!"
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "This is a matter of state. How can one show favor to a relative!"

sentences.zh: 」長仁竟坐死。

translations.literal: " Changren in the end was punished with death.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end Changren was put to death.

sentences.zh: 后異母弟陀，以猫鬼巫蠱，咒詛於后，坐當死。

translations.literal: The empress's younger half-brother Tuo, by means of cat-demon witchcraft and sorcery, cursed and imprecated against the empress, and for this offense was liable to death.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's younger half-brother Tuo used cat-demon witchcraft to curse her and was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 后三日不食，為之請命曰：「陀若蠧政害民者，妾不敢言。

translations.literal: For three days the empress ate nothing and pleaded for his life, saying: "If Tuo were one who harmed government and injured the people, your servant would not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: For three days the empress ate nothing and pleaded for his life, saying, "If Tuo had harmed the government or injured the people, I would not dare speak for him.

sentences.zh: 今坐為妾身，敢請其命。

translations.literal: Now he is punished on account of your servant's person—I venture to ask for his life."
translations.idiomatic: But he is punished only on my account, and I venture to ask for his life."

sentences.zh: 」陀於是減死一等。

translations.literal: " Tuo was thereby reduced one degree from death.
translations.idiomatic: " Tuo's sentence was reduced one degree from death.

sentences.zh: 后每與上言及政事，往往意合，宮中稱為二聖。

translations.literal: Whenever the empress spoke with the emperor about government affairs, their intentions often agreed, and within the palace they were called the Two Sages.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the empress discussed government with the emperor, their views often agreed, and within the palace they were called the Two Sages.

sentences.zh: 后頗仁愛，每聞大理決囚，未嘗不流涕。

translations.literal: The empress was quite benevolent; whenever she heard that the Court of Review had passed sentence on prisoners, she never failed to shed tears.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was compassionate by nature. Whenever she heard that the Court of Review had passed sentence on prisoners, she wept without fail.

sentences.zh: 然性尤妬忌，後宮莫敢進御。

translations.literal: Yet her nature was especially jealous, and none in the inner palace dared approach the emperor's bed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet she was fiercely jealous, and no woman in the inner palace dared share the emperor's bed.

sentences.zh: 尉遲迥女孫有美色，先在宮中。

translations.literal: A granddaughter of Yuwen Jiong had beautiful looks and was already in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: A granddaughter of Yuwen Jiong was exceptionally beautiful and was already in the palace.

sentences.zh: 上於仁壽宮見而悅之，因此得幸。

translations.literal: The emperor saw her at Renshou Palace and was pleased with her; through this she gained his favor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw her at Renshou Palace and was pleased with her, and through this she gained his favor.

sentences.zh: 后伺上聽朝，陰殺之。

translations.literal: The empress waited until the emperor was attending court and secretly killed her.
translations.idiomatic: The empress waited until the emperor was at court and secretly had her killed.

sentences.zh: 上由是大怒，單騎從苑中而出，不由徑路，入山谷間二十餘里。

translations.literal: The emperor was thereby greatly enraged. Alone on horseback he rode out of the park, not by the main path, and entered the mountain valleys for more than twenty li.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious. Alone on horseback he rode out of the park, left the main path, and plunged more than twenty li into the mountain valleys.

sentences.zh: 高熲、楊素等追及上，扣馬苦諫。

translations.literal: Gao Feng, Yang Su, and others overtook the emperor, seized his horse's bridle, and remonstrated with bitter earnestness.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Feng, Yang Su, and others overtook him, seized his horse's bridle, and remonstrated with him in desperate earnest.

sentences.zh: 上太息曰：「吾貴為天子，而不得自由！

translations.literal: The emperor sighed deeply and said: "I am exalted as Son of Heaven, yet I cannot be free!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed deeply and said, "I am exalted as Son of Heaven, yet I am not free!"

sentences.zh: 」高熲曰：「陛下豈以一婦人而輕天下！

translations.literal: " Gao Feng said: "Your Majesty, would you for a single woman slight the realm under Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Feng said, "Your Majesty, would you slight the realm under Heaven for the sake of one woman!"

sentences.zh: 」上意少解，駐馬良久，中夜方始還宮。

translations.literal: " The emperor's mind was somewhat eased; he halted his horse for a long while and only at midnight did he return to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor's anger eased a little. He halted his horse for a long while and did not return to the palace until midnight.

sentences.zh: 后俟上於閣內。

translations.literal: The empress waited for the emperor inside the gate-tower.
translations.idiomatic: The empress waited for him inside the gate-tower.

sentences.zh: 及上至，后流涕拜謝，熲、素等和解之。

translations.literal: When the emperor arrived, the empress wept and bowed in apology; Feng, Su, and the others reconciled them.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, the empress wept and bowed in apology. Feng, Su, and the others brought about a reconciliation.

sentences.zh: 上置酒極歡，后自此意頗衰折。

translations.literal: The emperor set out wine and they were extremely merry; from this time the empress's will was rather diminished and broken.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor set out wine and they made merry together, but from that time the empress's authority was noticeably diminished.

sentences.zh: 初，后以高熲是父之家客，甚見親禮。

translations.literal: At first, because Gao Feng had been a household guest of her father's house, the empress treated him with great intimacy and courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: At first, because Gao Feng had been a retainer in her father's household, the empress treated him with great intimacy and respect.

sentences.zh: 至是，聞熲謂己為一婦人，因此銜恨。

translations.literal: At this time, hearing that Feng had called her a mere woman, she therefore harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Now, hearing that Feng had called her a mere woman, she bore a deep grudge against him.

sentences.zh: 又以熲夫人死，其妾生男，益不善之，漸加譖毀，上亦每事唯后言是用。

translations.literal: Moreover, when Feng's principal wife died and his concubine bore a son, she thought even less well of him and gradually added slander and defamation; the emperor too in every matter followed only what the empress said.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng's principal wife died and his concubine bore a son, she thought even less of him and gradually slandered him to the emperor. The emperor, for his part, followed her word in almost every matter.

sentences.zh: 后見諸王及朝士有妾孕者，必勸上斥之。

translations.literal: Whenever the empress saw princes or court gentlemen whose concubines were pregnant, she would urge the emperor to dismiss them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever she saw a prince or court official whose concubine was pregnant, she urged the emperor to dismiss him.

sentences.zh: 時皇太子多內寵，妃元氏暴薨，后意太子愛妾雲氏害之。

translations.literal: At that time the crown prince had many inner favorites; the consort of the Yuan clan died suddenly, and the empress suspected that the crown prince's beloved concubine of the Yun clan had harmed her.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the crown prince kept many concubines. His consort of the Yuan clan died suddenly, and the empress suspected that the prince's beloved concubine, Lady Yun, had caused her death.

sentences.zh: 由是諷上黜高熲，竟廢太子立晉王廣，皆后之謀也。

translations.literal: Thereby she indirectly urged the emperor to dismiss Gao Feng, and in the end the crown prince was deposed and Prince of Jin Guang was established—all this was the empress's design.
translations.idiomatic: Through this she urged the emperor to dismiss Gao Feng, and in the end the crown prince was deposed and Prince Guang of Jin was made heir. All of this was the empress's doing.

sentences.zh: 仁壽二年八月甲子，月暈四重，己巳，太白犯軒轅。

translations.literal: In the second year of Renshou, on the jiazi day of the eighth month, the moon had halos within halos fourfold; on the jisi day, the Great White star encroached upon Xuanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Renshou, on the jiazi day of the eighth month, the moon showed fourfold halos; on the jisi day, Venus encroached upon the Xuanyuan constellation.

sentences.zh: 其夜，后崩於永安宮，時年五十。

translations.literal: That night the empress died at Yong'an Palace; she was then fifty.
translations.idiomatic: That night the empress died at Yong'an Palace at the age of fifty.

sentences.zh: 葬於太陵。

translations.literal: She was buried at Tailing.
translations.idiomatic: She was buried at Tailing.

sentences.zh: 其後，宣華夫人陳氏、容華夫人蔡氏俱有寵，上頗惑之，由是發疾。

translations.literal: Afterward Lady Xuanhua of the Chen clan and Lady Ronghua of the Cai clan both received favor; the emperor was rather bewildered by them, and from this illness arose.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward both Lady Xuanhua of the Chen clan and Lady Ronghua of the Cai clan won his favor. He was much taken with them, and from this he fell ill.

sentences.zh: 及危篤，謂侍者曰「使皇后在，吾不及此」云。

translations.literal: When he was critically ill, he told his attendants, "Had the empress still been alive, I would not have come to this," he said.
translations.idiomatic: When he was critically ill, he told his attendants, "Had the empress still been alive, I would not have come to this."

sentences.zh: 宣華夫人陳氏，陳宣帝之女也。

translations.literal: Lady Xuanhua of the Chen clan was a daughter of Emperor Xuan of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xuanhua of the Chen clan was a daughter of Emperor Xuan of Chen.

sentences.zh: 性聰慧，姿貌無雙。

translations.literal: By nature she was intelligent and clever, and in looks without peer.
translations.idiomatic: She was intelligent by nature and without peer in beauty.

sentences.zh: 及陳滅，配掖庭，後選入宮為嬪。

translations.literal: When Chen was destroyed, she was assigned to the palace women; later she was selected to enter the palace as a Pin.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell, she was assigned to the palace women, and later she was selected to enter the inner palace as a Pin.

sentences.zh: 時獨孤皇后性妬，後宮罕得進御，唯陳氏有寵。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Dugu was jealous by nature, and those in the inner palace rarely gained access to the emperor; only the Chen lady had favor.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Empress Dugu was fiercely jealous, and few women in the inner palace shared the emperor's bed. Only Lady Chen enjoyed his favor.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣之在藩也，陰有奪宗之計，規為內助，每致禮焉。

translations.literal: When Prince of Jin Guang was in his fief, he secretly had a plan to seize the succession and schemed to make her an inner helper; he often sent her gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Guang of Jin was in his fief, he secretly plotted to seize the succession and sought her help within the palace. He often sent her gifts.

sentences.zh: 進金蛇、金駝等物，以取媚於陳氏。

translations.literal: He presented golden snakes, golden camels, and other objects to win the Chen lady's favor.
translations.idiomatic: He sent her golden snakes, golden camels, and other gifts to win her favor.

sentences.zh: 皇太子廢立之際，頗有力焉。

translations.literal: At the time of the crown prince's deposition and establishment, she contributed considerable force.
translations.idiomatic: At the time of the crown prince's deposition and replacement, she exerted considerable influence.

sentences.zh: 及文獻皇后崩，進位為貴人，專房擅寵，主斷內事，六宮莫與為比。

translations.literal: When Empress Wenxian died, she was advanced to the rank of Noble Lady, monopolized the bedchamber and held favor alone, decided inner affairs, and none of the six palaces could compare with her.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wenxian died, Lady Chen was promoted to Noble Lady. She monopolized the emperor's favor, controlled affairs within the palace, and none of the six palaces could compare with her.

sentences.zh: 及上大漸，遺詔拜為宣華夫人。

translations.literal: When the emperor's illness grew grave, his final edict invested her as Lady Xuanhua.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor's illness grew grave, his final edict invested her as Lady Xuanhua.

sentences.zh: 初，上寢疾於仁壽宮也，夫人與皇太子同侍疾。

translations.literal: At first, when the emperor lay ill at Renshou Palace, the lady and the crown prince together attended his sickness.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when the emperor lay ill at Renshou Palace, Lady Xuanhua and the crown prince attended him together.

sentences.zh: 平旦出更衣，為太子所逼，夫人拒之得免，歸於上所。

translations.literal: At daybreak she went out to change her clothes and was pressed by the crown prince; the lady resisted and escaped, then returned to the emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak she went out to change her clothes and was accosted by the crown prince. She resisted and escaped, then returned to the emperor's bedside.

sentences.zh: 上怪其神色有異，問其故。

translations.literal: The emperor wondered at her altered expression and asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor noticed her altered expression and asked the reason.

sentences.zh: 夫人泫然曰：「太子無禮。

translations.literal: The lady said with tears: "The crown prince was without propriety."
translations.idiomatic: With tears in her eyes she said, "The crown prince behaved without propriety."

sentences.zh: 」上恚曰：「畜生何足付大事，獨孤誠誤我！

translations.literal: " The emperor said in anger: "That beast is not fit to be entrusted with great affairs—Dugu truly misled me!"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said in anger, "That beast is not fit to be entrusted with great affairs. Dugu truly misled me!"

sentences.zh: 」意謂獻皇后也。

translations.literal: " He meant Empress Xian.
translations.idiomatic: " He meant Empress Dugu.

sentences.zh: 因呼兵部尚書柳述、黃門侍郎元巖曰：「召我兒！

translations.literal: Thereupon he called Minister of War Liu Xu and Palace Attendant Yuan Yan and said: "Summon my son!"
translations.idiomatic: He then called Minister of War Liu Xu and Palace Attendant Yuan Yan and said, "Summon my son!"

sentences.zh: 」述等將呼太子，上曰：「勇也。

translations.literal: " Xu and the others were about to summon the crown prince; the emperor said: "Yong."
translations.idiomatic: " Xu and the others were about to summon the crown prince, but the emperor said, "Yong."

sentences.zh: 」述、巖出閤為勑書訖，示左僕射楊素。

translations.literal: " Xu and Yan went out of the gate-tower, completed the imperial order, and showed it to Left Director Yang Su.
translations.idiomatic: " Xu and Yan left the gate-tower, drafted the imperial order, and showed it to Left Director Yang Su.

sentences.zh: 素以其事白太子，太子遣張衡入寢殿，遂令夫人及後宮同侍疾者，並出就別室。

translations.literal: Su reported the matter to the crown prince; the crown prince sent Zhang Heng into the sleeping hall and then ordered the lady and all in the inner palace who were attending the sickness to go out to separate rooms.
translations.idiomatic: Su reported the matter to the crown prince. The crown prince sent Zhang Heng into the sleeping hall and ordered Lady Xuanhua and all the women of the inner palace who were attending the emperor to leave for separate rooms.

sentences.zh: 俄聞上崩，而未發喪也。

translations.literal: Soon they heard that the emperor had died, but mourning had not yet been proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they heard that the emperor had died, but the death had not yet been announced.

sentences.zh: 夫人與諸後宮相顧曰：「事變矣！

translations.literal: The lady and the women of the inner palace looked at one another and said: "Things have changed!"
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xuanhua and the other palace women looked at one another and said, "Things have changed!"

sentences.zh: 」皆色動股慄。

translations.literal: " All changed color and their thighs trembled.
translations.idiomatic: " All turned pale and trembled in their limbs.

sentences.zh: 晡後，太子遣使者齎金合子，帖紙於際，親署封字，以賜夫人。

translations.literal: After the hour of shen, the crown prince sent an envoy bearing a golden casket, with paper pasted at the seam and the seal characters written in his own hand, to bestow it upon the lady.
translations.idiomatic: In the afternoon the crown prince sent an envoy bearing a golden casket sealed with paper at the seam and inscribed in his own hand, to present it to Lady Xuanhua.

sentences.zh: 夫人見之惶懼，以為鴆毒，不敢發。

translations.literal: When the lady saw it she was fearful and afraid, thinking it poison, and did not dare open it.
translations.idiomatic: When she saw it she was terrified, thinking it contained poison, and did not dare open it.

sentences.zh: 使者促之，於是乃發，見合中有同心結數枚。

translations.literal: The envoy urged her, and only then did she open it and see several matching-knot ornaments inside the casket.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy urged her, and only then did she open it and find several matching-knot ornaments inside.

sentences.zh: 諸宮人咸悅，相謂曰：「得免死矣！

translations.literal: All the palace women were pleased and said to one another: "We have escaped death!"
translations.idiomatic: All the palace women rejoiced and said to one another, "We have escaped death!"

sentences.zh: 」陳氏恚而却坐，不肯致謝。

translations.literal: " The Chen lady was angry and drew back to sit, refusing to offer thanks.
translations.idiomatic: " Lady Chen was angry, drew back, and refused to offer thanks.

sentences.zh: 諸宮人共逼之，乃拜使者。

translations.literal: The palace women together pressed her, and only then did she bow to the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: The other palace women pressed her until she bowed to the envoy.

sentences.zh: 其夜，太子烝焉。

translations.literal: That night the crown prince took her in the forbidden union.
translations.idiomatic: That night the crown prince violated her.

sentences.zh: 及煬帝嗣位之後，出居仙都宮。

translations.literal: After Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, she went out to dwell at Xiandu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, she was sent to live at Xiandu Palace.

sentences.zh: 尋召入，歲餘而終，時年二十九。

translations.literal: Soon she was summoned back in; a little more than a year later she died, aged twenty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Soon she was summoned back to the palace, and a little more than a year later she died at the age of twenty-nine.

sentences.zh: 帝深悼之，為製神傷賦。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned her deeply and composed the Rhapsody of Spirit's Wounding for her.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned her deeply and composed the Rhapsody of Spirit's Wounding in her memory.

sentences.zh: 容華夫人蔡氏，丹陽人也。

translations.literal: Lady Ronghua of the Cai clan was a native of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Ronghua of the Cai clan was a native of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 陳滅之後，以選入宮，為世婦。

translations.literal: After Chen was destroyed, she was selected to enter the palace and became a Shifu.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of Chen she was selected for the palace and became a Shifu.

sentences.zh: 容儀婉嫕，上甚悅之。

translations.literal: Her bearing and appearance were gentle and lovely, and the emperor was greatly pleased with her.
translations.idiomatic: Her bearing was gentle and lovely, and the emperor was greatly pleased with her.

sentences.zh: 以文獻皇后故，希得進幸。

translations.literal: Because of Empress Wenxian, she rarely gained access to the emperor's bed.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Empress Wenxian, she rarely shared the emperor's bed.

sentences.zh: 及后崩，漸見寵遇，拜為貴人，參斷宮掖之務，與陳氏相亞。

translations.literal: When the empress died, she gradually received favor and was appointed Noble Lady, took part in deciding affairs of the inner palace, and was second only to the Chen lady.
translations.idiomatic: After the empress died, she gradually won favor, was appointed Noble Lady, took part in governing affairs within the palace, and stood second only to Lady Chen.

sentences.zh: 上寢疾，加號容華夫人。

translations.literal: When the emperor lay ill, she was given the additional title Lady Ronghua.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill, she was given the additional title Lady Ronghua.

sentences.zh: 上崩後，自請言事，亦為煬帝所烝。

translations.literal: After the emperor died, she herself asked to report a matter and was likewise taken in the forbidden union by Emperor Yang.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor's death she volunteered to report a matter and was likewise violated by Emperor Yang.

sentences.zh: 煬帝蕭皇后，梁明帝巋之女也。

translations.literal: Empress Xiao of Emperor Yang was a daughter of Emperor Ming of Liang, Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiao of Emperor Yang was a daughter of Emperor Ming of Liang, Xiao Kui.

sentences.zh: 江南風俗，二月生子者不舉。

translations.literal: In the customs of the south of the Yangzi, children born in the second month were not raised.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiangnan region, custom held that children born in the second month were not to be raised.

sentences.zh: 后以二月生，由是季父岌收而養之。

translations.literal: The empress was born in the second month; for this reason her father's younger brother Ji took her in and raised her.
translations.idiomatic: The future empress was born in the second month, and for this reason her uncle Ji took her in and raised her.

sentences.zh: 未幾，岌夫妻俱死，轉養舅氏張軻家。

translations.literal: Before long both Ji and his wife died, and she was transferred to be raised in the household of her mother's brother Zhang Ke.
translations.idiomatic: Before long both Ji and his wife died, and she was sent to be raised in the household of her uncle Zhang Ke.

sentences.zh: 然軻甚貧窶，后躬親勞苦。

translations.literal: Yet Ke was very poor and destitute, and the empress personally bore toil and hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ke was very poor, and the future empress labored with her own hands.

sentences.zh: 煬帝為晉王時，高祖將為王選妃於梁，遍占諸女，諸女皆不吉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang was Prince of Jin, the Founding Emperor was about to choose a consort for the prince in Liang; he divined for all the daughters, and all were inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Yang was Prince of Jin, Emperor Wen sought a bride for him in Liang. He cast lots for every daughter of the house, and every result was inauspicious.

sentences.zh: 巋迎后於舅氏，令使者占之，曰：「吉。

translations.literal: Kui brought the empress from her mother's brother's house and had the envoy divine for her; he said: "Auspicious."
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Kui brought her from her uncle's house and had the envoy cast lots for her. The result was auspicious.

sentences.zh: 」於是遂策為王妃。

translations.literal: " Thereupon she was established as the prince's consort.
translations.idiomatic: " She was then chosen as the prince's consort.

sentences.zh: 后性婉順，有智識，好學解屬文，頗知占候。

translations.literal: The empress's nature was gentle and compliant; she had wisdom and knowledge, loved learning and understood literary composition, and was quite versed in divination and observation of the heavens.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was gentle and compliant by nature, intelligent and well educated, skilled in literary composition, and versed in divination and astronomy.

sentences.zh: 高祖大善之，帝甚寵敬焉。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor greatly approved of her, and the emperor cherished and respected her deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen thought very highly of her, and her husband cherished and respected her deeply.

sentences.zh: 及帝嗣位，詔曰：「朕祗承丕緒，憲章在昔，爰建長秋，用承饗薦。

translations.literal: When the emperor succeeded to the throne, an edict said: "We respectfully receive the great succession; the statutes of old stand on record. We therefore establish the Eternal Autumn to undertake the offerings of sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: When he succeeded to the throne, an edict declared, "We respectfully receive the great succession. Following the statutes of old, We establish the office of the empress to preside over the sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 妃蕭氏，夙禀成訓，婦道克修，宜正位軒闈，式弘柔教，可立為皇后。」

translations.literal: Consort of the Xiao clan, from of old endowed with completed instruction, has fully cultivated the way of a wife—she should take the orthodox position in the inner gate and broadly extend gentle teaching; she may be established as empress."
translations.idiomatic: Consort Xiao has from childhood received proper instruction and fully cultivated the duties of a wife. She is fit to take the empress's place in the inner court and to extend gentle teaching throughout the realm. Let her be established as empress."

sentences.zh: 帝每遊幸，后未嘗不隨從。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor went on tour or excursion, the empress never failed to follow and attend.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor went on tour, the empress always accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 時后見帝失德，心知不可，不敢厝言，因為述志賦以自寄。

translations.literal: At that time the empress saw that the emperor had lost virtue, knew in her heart that nothing could be done, and did not dare set the matter aside in words; she therefore composed the Statement of Intent to lodge her feelings.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the empress saw that the emperor had lost his way. She knew in her heart that nothing could be done, yet dared not speak openly, and so composed the Statement of Intent to give voice to her feelings.

sentences.zh: 其詞曰：

translations.literal: Its words say:
translations.idiomatic: It reads:

sentences.zh: 承積善之餘慶，備箕箒於皇庭。

translations.literal: Receiving the surplus blessing of accumulated goodness, I was prepared with winnowing basket and broom in the imperial court.
translations.idiomatic: I received the lingering blessing of accumulated virtue and was made ready, winnowing basket and broom in hand, for service in the imperial court.

sentences.zh: 恐修名之不立，將負累於先靈。

translations.literal: I feared that a cultivated name would not be established and that I would bring burden upon the spirits of the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: I feared that I might fail to establish a worthy name and bring disgrace upon the spirits of my ancestors.

sentences.zh: 廼夙夜而匪懈，實寅懼於玄冥。

translations.literal: Therefore from morning to night without slackening, I truly held reverent fear toward the dark unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I labored from morning to night without slackening, ever in reverent awe of heaven's judgment.

sentences.zh: 雖自強而不息，亮愚矇之所滯。

translations.literal: Though I strengthened myself without ceasing, clearly the dull and benighted had their hindrances.
translations.idiomatic: Though I strove without ceasing, I knew how dull and limited my understanding was.

sentences.zh: 思竭節於天衢，才追心而弗逮。

translations.literal: I thought to exhaust my integrity upon heaven's highway, yet talent could not keep pace with the heart.
translations.idiomatic: I wished to give my utmost on heaven's highway, yet my talent could not keep pace with my heart.

sentences.zh: 實庸薄之多幸，荷隆寵之嘉惠。

translations.literal: Truly I was mediocre and slight yet greatly fortunate, bearing the fine favor of exalted grace.
translations.idiomatic: Mediocre and slight as I was, I had been greatly fortunate to receive the emperor's exalted favor.

sentences.zh: 賴天高而地厚，屬王道之升平。

translations.literal: Relying on heaven's height and earth's thickness, I belonged to the royal way's rising peace.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven was high and earth was broad, and I lived in an age when the royal way was at peace.

sentences.zh: 均二儀之覆載，與日月而齊明。

translations.literal: Equal with the two principles' covering and bearing, I shared brightness with sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: The two principles covered and sustained all things, and my lot was to share in the brightness of sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 廼春生而夏長，等品物而同榮。

translations.literal: Then spring was born and summer grew long; all kinds of things were equal and alike in glory.
translations.idiomatic: Spring gave birth and summer brought growth; all things flourished alike in glory.

sentences.zh: 願立志於恭儉，私自兢於誡盈。

translations.literal: I wished to set my will upon respectful frugality and privately to take warning against fullness.
translations.idiomatic: I resolved to live in respectful frugality and privately to guard against excess.

sentences.zh: 孰有念於知足，苟無希於濫名。

translations.literal: Who would keep thought of knowing sufficiency? I had scarcely any hope for inflated fame.
translations.idiomatic: I sought only to know when I had enough and desired no inflated fame.

sentences.zh: 惟至德之弘深，情不邇於聲色。

translations.literal: Only the utmost virtue was vast and deep; feeling did not draw near to sound and color.
translations.idiomatic: Only the utmost virtue was vast and deep; the heart did not linger on sound and color.

sentences.zh: 感懷舊之餘恩，求故劍於宸極。

translations.literal: Moved by the remaining grace of old affection, I sought the former sword at the imperial apex.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by the lingering grace of old affection, I sought the steadfast bond of the imperial marriage.

sentences.zh: 叨不世之殊盼，謬非才而奉職。

translations.literal: I presumptuously received an unworldly special regard and wrongly, without talent, undertook office.
translations.idiomatic: I had presumptuously received a regard beyond this world and, though without true talent, wrongly undertook my office.

sentences.zh: 何寵祿之踰分，撫胸襟而未識。

translations.literal: How did favor and emolument exceed my measure? I stroked my breast and did not understand.
translations.idiomatic: How had favor and rank exceeded my deserts? I pressed my hand to my breast and could not understand.

sentences.zh: 雖沐浴於恩光，內慚惶而累息。

translations.literal: Though I bathed in gracious light, inwardly I was ashamed and fearful, sighing again and again.
translations.idiomatic: Though I bathed in gracious light, inwardly I was ashamed and afraid, and sighed again and again.

sentences.zh: 顧微躬之寡昧，思令淑之良難。

translations.literal: Looking back on my slight person and scant understanding, I thought how hard it was to be truly good and fair.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on my slight person and scant understanding, I knew how hard it was to be truly virtuous.

sentences.zh: 實不遑於啟處，將何情而自安！

translations.literal: Truly I had no leisure to rise and sit—what feeling could bring me peace!
translations.idiomatic: I truly had no leisure for rest—what peace could my heart know!

sentences.zh: 若臨深而履薄，心戰慄其如寒。

translations.literal: As if facing a depth and treading on thin ice, my heart trembled in battle as though in cold.
translations.idiomatic: As if facing an abyss and treading on thin ice, my heart trembled as though in bitter cold.

sentences.zh: 夫居高而必危，慮處滿而防溢。

translations.literal: To dwell on high is necessarily perilous; one considers being full and guards against overflow.
translations.idiomatic: To stand on high is to stand in peril; one who is full must guard against overflowing.

sentences.zh: 知恣夸之非道，乃攝生於沖謐。

translations.literal: Knowing that wanton boasting is not the way, I then gathered life in emptiness and stillness.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that wanton boasting is not the way, I sought to preserve my life in quiet simplicity.

sentences.zh: 嗟寵辱之易驚，尚無為而抱一。

translations.literal: Alas, how easily favor and disgrace startle one; I still honored non-action and embraced the One.
translations.idiomatic: Alas, how easily favor and disgrace startle the heart; I still honored quietude and held fast to the One.

sentences.zh: 履謙光而守志，且願安乎容膝。

translations.literal: Treading modest light and keeping my will, I wished only to be at peace within knees' breadth of room.
translations.idiomatic: I walked in modest light and kept my will, wishing only to be at peace in a room no larger than my knees.

sentences.zh: 珠簾玉箔之奇，金屋瑤臺之美，雖時俗之崇麗，蓋吾人之所鄙。

translations.literal: The marvel of pearl curtains and jade foil, the beauty of golden chambers and jasper terraces—though the fashion of the age honored splendor, these were what we despised.
translations.idiomatic: Pearl curtains, jade screens, golden chambers, and jasper terraces—though the age honored such splendor, they were what I despised.

sentences.zh: 愧絺綌之不工，豈絲竹之喧耳。

translations.literal: Ashamed that my fine and coarse hemp garments were not well made, how could I welcome the clamor of strings and bamboo in my ears?
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed that my plain garments were poorly made, how could I welcome the clamor of strings and pipes in my ears?

sentences.zh: 知道德之可尊，明善惡之由己。

translations.literal: I knew that moral power may be honored and understood that good and evil arise from oneself.
translations.idiomatic: I knew that virtue deserves honor and understood that good and evil arise from oneself.

sentences.zh: 蕩囂煩之俗慮，乃伏膺於經史。

translations.literal: I swept away vulgar cares of clamor and trouble and then bowed my breast to the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: I swept away vulgar cares and bowed my heart to the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 綜箴誡以訓心，觀女圖而作軌。

translations.literal: I gathered admonitions and warnings to instruct the heart and viewed the pictures of women to make my track.
translations.idiomatic: I gathered admonitions to instruct my heart and studied the portraits of worthy women to set my course.

sentences.zh: 遵古賢之令範，冀福祿之能綏。

translations.literal: Following the fine models of ancient worthies, I hoped that fortune and emolument might be pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Following the fine models of the ancients, I hoped that fortune and blessing might be secured in peace.

sentences.zh: 時循躬而三省，覺今是而昨非。

translations.literal: At times I examined my person and thrice reflected, perceiving that today was right and yesterday wrong.
translations.idiomatic: At times I examined myself and reflected again and again, seeing that what is right today was wrong yesterday.

sentences.zh: 嗤黃老之損思，信為善之可歸。

translations.literal: I scoffed at Huang-Lao's diminishing of thought and trusted that doing good could bring return.
translations.idiomatic: I scoffed at Huang-Lao's distrust of active thought and trusted that doing good would bring its reward.

sentences.zh: 慕周姒之遺風，美虞妃之聖則。

translations.literal: I admired the lingering wind of Si of Zhou and praised the sage rule of the consort of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: I admired the legacy of Si of Zhou and praised the sacred example of the consort of Shun.

sentences.zh: 仰先哲之高才，貴至人之休德。

translations.literal: I looked up to the lofty talent of former sages and honored the beautiful virtue of perfected persons.
translations.idiomatic: I looked up to the lofty talent of the sages of old and honored the beautiful virtue of the perfected.

sentences.zh: 質菲薄而難蹤，心恬愉而去惑。

translations.literal: My substance was slight and hard to trace, yet my heart was calm and pleased and cast off confusion.
translations.idiomatic: My substance was slight and hard to match, yet my heart was calm and cast off confusion.

sentences.zh: 乃平生之耿介，實禮義之所遵。

translations.literal: This was the uprightness of my whole life—truly what ritual and righteousness command one to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the uprightness of my whole life—truly what ritual and righteousness command.

sentences.zh: 雖生知之不敏，庶積行以成仁。

translations.literal: Though innate knowing was not keen in me, I hoped that accumulated conduct might accomplish humaneness.
translations.idiomatic: Though I was not gifted with innate wisdom, I hoped that accumulated conduct might lead me to humaneness.

sentences.zh: 懼達人之蓋寡，謂何求而自陳。

translations.literal: Fearing that those who understand may be few, what did I seek in laying myself bare?
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that those who understand may be few, why did I lay myself bare in these words?

sentences.zh: 誠素志之難寫，同絕筆於獲麟。

translations.literal: Truly my plain will was hard to write down, like laying down the brush when the qilin was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Truly my plain intent was hard to set down, like laying down the brush when the qilin was captured.

sentences.zh: 及帝幸江都，臣下離貳，有宮人白后曰：「外聞人人欲反。

translations.literal: When the emperor favored Jiangdu, his ministers and subordinates were divided in loyalty, and a palace woman reported to the empress: "Outside one hears that everyone wishes to rebel."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went to Jiangdu, his officials grew disloyal, and a palace woman told the empress, "Outside, everyone says the people wish to rebel."

sentences.zh: 」后曰：「任汝奏之。

translations.literal: " The empress said: "As you wish—report it."
translations.idiomatic: " The empress said, "Then report it as you wish."

sentences.zh: 」宮人言於帝，帝大怒曰：「非所宜言！

translations.literal: " The palace woman told the emperor; the emperor said in great anger: "This is not what should be spoken!"
translations.idiomatic: " The palace woman told the emperor. He flew into a rage and said, "That is not what should be spoken!"

sentences.zh: 」遂斬之。

translations.literal: " He then beheaded her.
translations.idiomatic: " He had her beheaded at once.

sentences.zh: 後人復白后曰：「宿衞者往往偶語謀反。

translations.literal: Later someone again reported to the empress: "Those on night guard often speak together in pairs, plotting rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: Later someone again told the empress, "The night guards are often heard whispering together about rebellion."

sentences.zh: 」后曰：「天下事一朝至此，勢已然，無可救也。

translations.literal: " The empress said: "Affairs under heaven have in a morning come to this—the momentum is already set, and nothing can save them.
translations.idiomatic: " The empress said, "Affairs under heaven have come to this in a single morning. The momentum is already set, and nothing can save us.

sentences.zh: 何用言之，徒令帝憂煩耳。

translations.literal: What use is there in speaking of it? It would only make the emperor worried and troubled."
translations.idiomatic: What use is there in speaking of it? It would only add to the emperor's grief."

sentences.zh: 」自是無復言者。

translations.literal: " From this time there was no one who spoke again.
translations.idiomatic: " From that time on, no one spoke of it again.

sentences.zh: 及宇文氏之亂，隋軍至聊城。

translations.literal: When the disorder of the Yuwen clan broke out, Sui troops reached Liaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: When the disorders of the Yuwen clan broke out, Sui troops reached Liaocheng.

sentences.zh: 化及敗，沒於竇建德。

translations.literal: Huaji was defeated and she fell into the hands of Dou Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaji was defeated, she fell into the hands of Dou Jiande.

sentences.zh: 突厥處羅可汗遣使迎后於洺州，建德不敢留，遂入於虜庭。

translations.literal: Chuluo Qaghan of the Turks sent an envoy to welcome the empress at Mozhou; Jiande did not dare detain her, and she thereupon entered the barbarian court.
translations.idiomatic: Chuluo Qaghan of the Turks sent an envoy to receive the empress at Mozhou. Jiande did not dare detain her, and she passed into the Turkic court.

sentences.zh: 大唐貞觀四年，破滅突厥，乃以禮致之，歸于京師。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenguan of Great Tang, when the Turks were destroyed and extinguished, she was received with ritual propriety and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhenguan of the Tang, when the Turks were destroyed, she was received with due ceremony and returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：二后，帝未登庸，早儷宸極，恩隆好合，始終不渝。

translations.literal: The historian says: The two empresses, before the emperors had ascended to office, early became consorts of the imperial apex; their grace was lofty and their union good, unchanging from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Both empresses became imperial consorts while their husbands were still princes, and the bond between them was deep and unchanging from first to last.

sentences.zh: 文獻德異鳲鳩，心非均一，擅寵移嫡，傾覆宗社，惜哉！

translations.literal: Wenxian's virtue differed from the osprey; her heart was not evenly one. Monopolizing favor, she shifted the heir and overturned the ancestral altars—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Wenxian's virtue fell short of that praised in the Ospreys; her heart was not even-handed. She monopolized favor, displaced the rightful heir, and brought ruin upon the dynasty—alas!

sentences.zh: 書曰：「牝雞之晨，惟家之索。

translations.literal: The Documents say: "When the hen crows at dawn, the house is brought to ruin."
translations.idiomatic: The Documents say, "When the hen crows at dawn, the household is brought to ruin."

sentences.zh: 」高祖之不能敦睦九族，抑有由矣。

translations.literal: " That the Founding Emperor could not make his nine kindreds harmonious and close likewise had its reason.
translations.idiomatic: " That Emperor Wen could not keep his kinsmen in harmony likewise had its cause.

sentences.zh: 蕭后初歸藩邸，有輔佐君子之心。

translations.literal: When Empress Xiao first came to the prince's residence, she had a heart to assist the gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Xiao first entered the prince's household, she had the heart of one who would assist a worthy ruler.

sentences.zh: 煬帝得不以道，便謂人無忠信。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang gained the throne not by the proper way and thereupon supposed that people had no loyalty or faith.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang gained the throne by improper means and thereafter believed that no one could be loyal or trustworthy.

sentences.zh: 父子之間，尚懷猜阻，夫婦之際，其何有焉！

translations.literal: Between father and son he still harbored suspicion and obstruction—what could there be between husband and wife!
translations.idiomatic: Between father and son he still harbored suspicion and distrust—what bond could remain between husband and wife!

sentences.zh: 暨乎國破家亡，竄身無地，飄流異域，良足悲矣！

translations.literal: When at last the state was broken and the house destroyed, she had no place to hide her person and drifted in a foreign land—truly enough to grieve one!
translations.idiomatic: When at last the state was ruined and her house destroyed, she had nowhere to hide and drifted in a foreign land—a fate truly pitiable enough to break the heart!
